itemListElement.name: WordPress Speed & SEO Checklist 2026: Score Your Site in 2 Minutes

mainEntity.name: Why is my WordPress site so slow?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually a stack of small causes: cheap shared hosting, a heavy theme, too many plugins, unoptimised images and no caching. Hosting and caching are typically the biggest wins — fix those first.

mainEntity.name: Does site speed really affect Google rankings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — Core Web Vitals are part of Google's page-experience ranking signals, and slow pages also convert worse even when they do rank. Speed is both an SEO and a revenue issue.

mainEntity.name: How many plugins is too many?

acceptedAnswer.text: There's no magic number — 15 lean, well-built plugins beat 5 bloated ones. The real rule: every active plugin must earn its place, and overlapping plugins should be consolidated.

mainEntity.name: Will a rebuild hurt my existing Google rankings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if it's done carelessly. Preserving URL structure — or 301-redirecting every old URL to its new equivalent — carries your rankings across. Skipping that step is the most common self-inflicted SEO disaster.

mainEntity.name: Can you fix my slow WordPress site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — speed fixes, migrations and SEO-preserving rebuilds are core services. Run the audit, then book a free call and bring your score.
